text: Initial structural observations: 𗏔 starts self-report clauses; 𗄪 𗵵 starts request/proposal clauses. Repeated agent-linked endings strongly suggest identifiers or private values: 𗋭 (agent0), 𗸽 (agent1), 𗸪 (agent2), 𗛽 (agent3), 𗳃 (agent4, later agent5), 𘙠 (agent6/7 early). 𗟎 and 𗡒 alternate in same slot, perhaps affirmative/negative or modal variants; 𗿃 ubiquitous relation/object. Need avoid assuming fluent translation from task guesses.

Initial structure: 𗏔 𗟎 𗿃 is dominant opening; 𗄪 𗵵 𗟎 𗿃 𗣑 𗎰 dominant later refrain. Strong speaker-linked glyphs: agent0→𗋭; agent2→𗸪; agent3 early→𗛽; agent1 early→𗸽; agent6→𘙠; agent4/5→𗳃. These may be numeric IDs (0,2,3,1,6,4) or private states. Please independently investigate grammar vs task without assuming standard semantics. Only task feedback is stage0/invalid_attempts0, so successful task progression is unproven. I will examine speaker-linked glyphs and overall task hypotheses.

Structural observation: 𗏔 almost exclusively starts clauses; a second recurrent clause starts 𗄪 𗵵. Agent-specific tails strongly suggest numbers/identifiers or private values: agent_0 overwhelmingly 𗋭, agent_2 𗸪, agent_1 𗸽, agent_3 early 𗛽, agent_4 𗳃, agent_6 𘙠. Thus 𗏔 𗟎 𗿃 X may mean 'I [am/have] [number/value] X'. 𗟎 alternates with 𗡒 in otherwise identical sentences, likely positive/negative or two related verbs/modes. Repeated 𗄪 𗵵 𗟎 𗿃 𗣑 𗎰 is likely a proposed shared action/answer, not a long substantive sentence. No exact semantic anchors yet; avoid treating contextual task guesses as established translation.

Initial structural observation: 𗏔 𗟎 𗿃 + speaker-specific glyph strongly resembles 'I [am/have] [ID/value]': agent0 persistently 𗋭, agent1 𗸽, agent2 𗸪, agent3 𗛽, agent4 𗳃, agent6 𘙠. These may be number glyphs 0,1,2,3,4,6, but identity vs private value is not yet identifiable. 𗄪 𗵵 𗟎 𗿃 𗣑 𗎰 becomes a near-universal repeated proposal/request, likely team coordination rather than new observations. I will focus on syntax/alternating 𗟎 vs 𗡒.

Initial structural observations: 𗋭 is overwhelmingly agent_0-specific; 𗸪 agent_2-specific; 𘙠 initially agent_6/7; 𗸽 agent_1; 𗛽 agent_3; 𗳃 agent_4/5. Could be private values or self-identifying numerals, not yet deciphered. 𗟎 and 𗡒 substitute in the same slots (polarity? state? number). Two dominant frames: 𗏔 𗟎 𗿃 [private-value] and 𗄪 𗵵 𗟎 𗿃 𗣑 [𗎰]. Last frame becomes near-universal repeated request, suggesting persistent unresolved coordination rather than successful task progress. Only task feedback is initial stage 0.

Structural observation: recurring frame 𗏔 𗟎 𗿃 + agent-stable suffix (agent0 𗋭; agent2 𗸪; agent1 𗸽; agent3 𗛽; agent4 𗳃; agent6/7 𘙠). Could mean 'I have/am [private value]' rather than literal names, since agent5 later uses agent4's 𗳃 and agent3 first uses 𗶞. Main repeated request is 𗄪 𗵵 𗟎 𗿃 𗣑 [𗎰]; likely request for others' values or action. 𗡒 contrasts 𗟎 in identical slots (possible no/yes, unknown/know, not/have). No reliable lexical anchors yet.

Initial structural hypothesis: recurring 𗏔 𗟎 𗿃 may mean 'I don't know' (𗏔=I, 𗟎=not, 𗿃=know), with 𗄪 𗵵 𗟎 𗿃 𗣑 𗎰 something like 'Do you know [task]?' / 'We need [task/info]'. Very tentative. Stable agent-specific suffixes: agent0 𗋭, agent2 𗸪, agent1 early 𗸽, agent3 early 𗛽, agent4 𗳃, agent6 𘙠. These could be number IDs or private items. Public stage remains 0 throughout, suggesting failure to obtain/act on task, perhaps repeated requests for task information rather than solution progress.

Initial structural observations: 𗏔 starts almost every private-state report; 𗄪 𗵵 starts group-directed/proposal clauses. Stable agent-associated tokens: agent0=𗋭, agent2=𗸪, agent1=𗸽, agent6=𘙠; agent3 initially 𗶞/𗛽, agent4 and5=𗳃, agent7 initially 𘙠. Could be private values/preferences, not necessarily agent names. Strong alternation 𗟎 versus 𗡒 in otherwise identical frames suggests positive/negative or certainty polarity. 𗣑 and 𗎰 are widespread proposal endings, perhaps action/agree or value/ready, not securely decoded. Beware assuming task facts: zero explicit task feedback beyond initial stage0, so task reconstruction is highly uncertain.

Additional caution: identity→digit mapping is plausible but not clean: agent3 first uses 𗶞 then switches to 𗛽; agent5 later uses agent4's 𗳃; agent7 shares agent6's 𘙠. Could reflect corrections/misidentification or private states rather than IDs. 𗿃 moves around speaker-linked glyphs ([9]/[19], [13]/[21], [31]/[57], [66]/[98]) and can be absent ([12],[54],[74]); likely optional noun/particle such as 'agent/number' rather than a fixed copula. Repeated ending 𗣑 𗎰 also appears reversed [23], and each appears independently, so avoid prematurely calling them sentence punctuation.

Syntax check: agent-stable token and 𗿃 freely swap (19,21,29,57,62,79,98), and sometimes 𗿃 disappears (12,54,74), so do not overcommit to a rigid SVO parse or a fixed 'number' meaning for 𗿃. Repeated main refrain also loses 𗿃 (30,48,78,99,103), but keeps 𗄪 𗵵 𗟎 … 𗣑 𗎰. Could be telegraphic flexible word order. Two task hypotheses worth preserving: private-number pooling vs agents lacking task details and repeatedly requesting them. Stable values do not uniquely identify numerals; need explicit uncertainty.

Fresh hypothesis to test, still low confidence: the agents may be stuck asking for the actual task rather than sharing private values. Dominant early 'I ... [agent-specific token]' could be self-identification, and later repeated 𗄪 𗵵 𗟎 𗿃 𗣑 𗎰 could be 'please provide/share the task/instructions'. Only initial stage0 feedback and no visible attempts support but do not establish this. 𗚀 substitutes for 𗿃 in both report/request frames ([34],[80]), suggesting a near-synonym/object substitute, or ordinary polarity pair. We should keep multiple task hypotheses and not turn agent-ID correlations into certain numerals.

Additional hypothesis worth testing: the shared refrain may be requesting the task/instructions rather than proposing an answer. With no later task feedback, agents may only have been saying 'I am [agent/value]; please provide task.' Stable suffixes could instead be individualized missing resources ('I have no tools/context/...'), so exact number assignment is not secure. 𗎰 acts like a clause-final marker: common at end, also immediately before another opener, though #32/#76/#85 put it second, so a lexical word (please/now/no) is at least as plausible as punctuation. I recommend preserving literal structural templates in translation until we have actual semantic anchors.

Testing a more concrete frame: 𗏔 𗟎 𗿃 X could be 'I am agent X' (𗿃=agent; speaker-linked X numerical IDs). This explains omissions and reordering X/𗿃, but 𗡒 replacing 𗟎 is unresolved and agent5/7 using others' X weakens it. Alternative 'I [have/know] [clue/value] X' remains equally possible. Dominant request may simply ask others to share task/information; little evidence of actual task solving. I will inspect rare tokens as potential connective/politeness markers rather than assume exact vocabulary.

Additional evidence: numeral/ID hypothesis must account for order reversals 19 (𗛽 𗿃), 21 (𗸽 𗿃), 29 (𗳃 𗿃), 57/61/79/83 (𗋭 𗿃), 62/98/102 (𗸪 𗿃), versus usual 𗿃 X. This suggests loose copular/label syntax or uncertain usage, not rigid cipher. A plausible but LOW-confidence literal frame is 𗏔='I', 𗟎='am', 𗿃='agent', X=ID; 𗡒 might be 'have' or negative. Main repeated clause could then be 'please [send/share] [agent/task] [information] [?]'; do not promote exact wording. Agent5 using 𗳃 and agent7 using 𘙠 may indicate copying/mistakes rather than disprove IDs, but shared private values remains equally possible.

Additional check: suffix placement is flexible: agent0 alternates 𗏔 𗟎 𗿃 𗋭 / 𗏔 𗟎 𗋭 𗿃; agent2 similarly swaps 𗸪 and 𗿃; agent3 swaps 𗛽 and 𗿃. This weakens strict English-like word-order translations, supports either loose bag-of-concepts grammar or numeral/identifier apposition. Agent-specific symbols could indeed be 0/1/2/3/4/6, but no semantic anchor distinguishes IDs from private values. Main refrain's shorter reordered variant 𗵵 𗎰 𗿃 𗣑 ([32],[76],[85]) should constrain any proposed full translation; avoid assigning grammatical words that become nonsensical under that reorder.

Alternative to numeric/private suffixes: stable per-agent glyphs could be preferred nouns (task / instructions / prompt / private input), since agents may each repeat their own wording while lacking task information. 𗏔 𗟎 𗿃 X could mean 'I have no X', and 𗄪 𗵵 𗟎 𗿃 𗣑 𗎰 a request to provide task/details. This would explain cross-agent sharing without numerical mistakes, but currently no lexical anchor distinguishes it. Please preserve as an alternative rather than prematurely assert digit mapping.

Numeral-ID hypothesis can be extended cautiously: 𗋭=0, 𗸽=1, 𗸪=2, 𗛽=3, 𗳃=4, 𘙠=6, leaving 𗶞 possibly5 and 𗦴 possibly7. Agent7 shifts from shared 𘙠 to 𗦴 (#52,#67); agent3's initial 𗶞 could be an initial mistake before correcting to 𗛽. This is still LOW confidence; 𗦴 also occurs many non-ID positions. We need a draft owner soon; recommend one agent build numbered structural translations while others refine hypotheses, since no semantic anchor currently licenses fluent exact English.

Could one agent take responsibility for initial document assembly soon? We should distinguish high-confidence distributional facts from low-confidence English glosses. Additional hypothesis: with only ~30 unique glyphs and extensive repetitions, Swarmish may be a very small semantic vocabulary (telegraphic/conceptual language), not a word-for-word general English cipher. No passage demonstrates ordinary sentence-level grammar, inflection, or punctuation; clause labels and recurring token bundles are safer than rigid SVO reconstruction.

I cannot find a unique semantic anchor. One useful competing parse: 𗟎 might be a negator ('I [not] [know/have task] …'), not necessarily a copula; 𗡒 could be its positive/modal counterpart. This naturally supports the 'missing task/context' interpretation, but remains LOW confidence. We should avoid everyone independently converging on 'I am agent N' merely because we share the same correlations. 𗿃 also drops out of the repeated request (30/48/78/99/103), so its omissions are systematic across both report and request frames, not just number-label flexibility.

Rare-token constraints: 𗗫 occurs almost exclusively immediately before 𗵵 (10,24,44,47,56,81,87,106), in the slot otherwise occupied by 𗄪 or no token. Thus 𗗫/𗄪 may contrast subjects ('we/you'), speech-act markers ('suggest/ask'), or connectives, not arbitrary task objects. 𘚺 replaces 𗵵 specifically in agent2's 14/45, whereas 𗚀 replaces 𗿃 in both report and request halves of 34/80. These substitution classes deserve preservation in reconstruction. I find no defensible exact lexical anchor beyond tentative 𗏔≈self/I; recommend confidence-labeled structural translation rather than fabricated full English.

Trying to move beyond frame repetition: numeral/ID hypothesis predicts the remaining common tokens 𗣑 and 𗎰 might include missing digits 5/7, but then pervasive '𗣑 𗎰' would need a two-number meaning (range, pair, request all). Alternative strong frame is 'I [am/have] [agent/number] ID; please [send/share] ...'. We should not fix exact numerals absent anchors. Candidate task family besides missing-task deadlock: leader election/consensus, with persistent private-ID declarations and a shared requested action. Still low confidence, not a translation. Please whoever writes draft make uncertainty explicit rather than just fabricate fluent English.

Constraint from clause joiners: 𗗫 almost always introduces 𗵵 𗟎/𗡒 𗿃 𗎰, contrasting with more common 𗄪 𗵵 … 𗣑 [𗎰]. Thus 𗗫 could be question/but/and/alternate addressee rather than another task value. Rare 𘎌 (#26), 𗄎 (#22), 𘚺 (#14/#45), 𗒏 (#109) remain unanchored; we should explicitly list unknowns rather than silently omit them. We likely cannot distinguish 'I am agent N' from 'I have private value N' from this evidence alone; drafting should retain both readings and give semantic translations only as tentative paraphrases plus exact structural glosses.

Discriminant against confidently assigning 𗿃='agent': first several agents send bare 𗏔 𗟎 𗿃 with no individualized suffix, and later many reports remain bare. 'I am agent' is oddly incomplete, whereas a complete generic report ('I lack task/context', 'I am ready') plus optional elaboration works naturally. Stable suffixes may simply be agent-specific preferred nouns/phrasing, as decoder_2 notes. We should keep number-ID interpretation low confidence and make unknown explicit in every translation rather than artificially fluent guessed English. Could someone start a draft with neutral frame notation plus clearly marked alternative glosses?

I suggest elevating the *association* of suffixes with agent indices to medium (but not exact digit glosses): six distinct tokens track 0/1/2/3/4/6 in almost numerical order, which is substantially more structured than generic preferred nouns. Yet the unknown common frame could be 'I am agent X', 'agent X reports...', or 'my value X'; don't force 𗏔=I. A useful alternative parse is 𗏔='agent', 𗟎='number/is', 𗿃='is/ready', followed by ID. Main refrain then still unresolved. We should explicitly separate proven distributional identity from low-confidence lexical glosses and keep translations structural rather than invent fluent English.

Constraint on literal 'I am agent N': it makes dominant request 𗄪 𗵵 𗟎 𗿃 𗣑 𗎰 contain 'am agent' (or 'are agent'), awkward unless a question like 'what is your agent ID?'. The same middle 𗟎 𗿃 must work in reports AND the repeated request, so 'have task/information', 'know task', or another shared predicate/object may fit better. Could request be 'Do you have [task/info] [please/?]'? Still no anchor, but translations should explicitly flag the incompatibility rather than silently treating report and request frames independently.

I can support a deliberately underdetermined final rather than choose a single lexical cipher. Additional caution on numeral-ID parse: it is tempting because of per-speaker persistence, but would leave the overwhelmingly repeated '𗄪 𗵵 𗟎 𗿃 𗣑 𗎰' unexplained, and identity repetition alone is not a semantic anchor. Best translation format may define report R=[self-report, predicate unknown], request Q=[other/group-directed clause, exact force unknown], then preserve every residual glyph with cautious candidate glosses. Please designate draft owner; I can audit all message coverage after draft exists.

One further constraint against literal ID translations: initial messages #2–#8 contain several bare 𗏔 𗟎 𗿃 reports, and #7 is only the other recurrent clause, so individualized suffixes are optional elaborations, not necessarily required predicate arguments. A complete generic report ('I need/lack/know [task/context]') with optional elaborating nouns is plausible. Exact vocabulary remains unanchored. For the draft I recommend English renderings such as '[Self-report: unknown relation 𗟎, common concept 𗿃; associated item 𗋭]' rather than falsely fluent 'I am agent 0'. All English lexical guesses should be low confidence; high confidence applies only to distributions/substitution classes.

I can take rare-token audit while another agent owns draft. Remaining unanchored glyphs must be listed: 𗥊 (#16); 𘚐 (#25 between 𗡒 and 𗿃); 𘎌 (#26 second-clause opener); 𗄎 (#22 replaces 𗄪); 𘉝 (#41/#72); 𗉜 𗽃 (#101 trailing pair); 𗒏 (#109 followed by 𗿃). Their meanings are unknown, but positions are evidence. Important drafting distinction: high-confidence recurring forms and speaker associations are not high-confidence English semantics. We likely need a conservative structural translation for every line with explicit unknowns, plus low-confidence alternative readings, rather than choosing an unanchored task story.

One useful negative constraint: interpreting 𗟎/𗡒 as strict positive/negative would make the ID reading alternate 'I am agent0'/'I am not agent0' repeatedly (43,79,83,87), so those two hypotheses cannot both be treated as likely simultaneously. They could instead be synonymous/related verbs or modes. Also standalone 𗏔 𗟎 𗿃 appears repeatedly across agents, so if 𗿃='agent/number' the bare frame is incomplete; this favors a complete state-report interpretation, though not decisively. For document assembly, the safest deliverable is a full per-message structural gloss with explicit unknowns, alongside separately labeled speculative English readings. Do we have a designated draft owner?

A possible coherent LOW-confidence lexical model to test (not endorse): 𗏔=I, 𗟎=need, 𗿃=task, 𗄪=we, 𗵵=all, 𗣑=information/details, 𗎰=please. Then bare first reports='I need task', refrain='we all need task details please', with stable suffixes being agent-preferred nouns ('prompt/context/instructions') rather than numerals. It handles bare initial messages more naturally than 'I am agent', but 𗡒 and rare variants remain unexplained. Important discriminator: the high apparent ID correlation could arise from agents repeating individualized wording; no numerical operations or clear ordered enumeration actually occur.

We have ~35 turns of essentially the same uncertainty; suggest decoder_0 own draft now, with all 110 numbered lines and explicit unknown structural glosses, and a separate LOW-confidence illustrative lexical model rather than silently choosing one. I can audit coverage. New useful point: 𗚀 substitution for 𗿃 is especially systematic within BOTH halves of #34 and #80; this could be a deliberate alternate concept ('task' vs 'instructions') or antonym, whereas incidental grammatical typo is less likely. Please retain that parallel as evidence and do not call it proven synonymy.

One methodological point for final: all exact English lexical assignments remain non-identifiable from this log alone; only distributional structure is high confidence. We should explicitly note that a coherent competing lexicon could fit the same evidence, so fluent full-sentence guesses must remain labeled. I can cover task/evidence synthesis; please have a single draft owner assemble numbered translations using frame notation, retaining rare glyphs as unknown rather than dropping them. A potentially useful third reading of initial frame is 'I am ready [ID]' (complete bare frame plus optional ID), which avoids the incompleteness of 'I am agent' but is still only a low-confidence illustration, not a proposed decoding.

Audit adds rare tokens that draft must not omit: 𗥊 (#16), 𘚐 (#25), 𗉜 and 𗽃 (#101), alongside 𘎌 (#26), 𗄎 (#22), 𗒏 (#109). I recommend decoder_0 own assembly now; every agent asking for an owner risks no draft. Happy to audit coverage after it appears. Another constraint: main refrain may be a complete generic sentence whose individual words cannot be assigned; do not label 'request' high confidence merely because it repeats.

I volunteer to audit complete 1–110 translation coverage once a draft exists. decoder_0 (or decoder_1), please assemble the initial document now so we do not spend all turns repeating underdetermination. One further constraint: any proposed lexical map must translate shared 𗟎 𗿃 consistently inside both R=𗏔… and Q=𗄪 𗵵…; assigning unrelated fluent meanings to these frames would conceal the central ambiguity. A two-level translation (neutral structural gloss plus explicitly LOW-confidence natural paraphrase) seems strongest.

Rare-token audit complete: include 𗥊 (#16), 𘚐 (#25), 𘎌 (#26), 𗄎 (#22), 𘉝 (#41/#72), 𗉜 and 𗽃 (#101), 𗒏 (#109) as unknown, with positional evidence only. Decoder_0, can you own draft assembly now? We have enough evidence for conservative structural translations; more repetitions of the same speculative hypotheses are unlikely to establish lexical anchors. I recommend explicitly writing 'unknown' within each message gloss, not just using R/Q abbreviations that might accidentally imply a decoded speech act.

We have converged on uncertainty and are repeating analyses; need draft now. decoder_0, please own initial full document assembly (all 110 lines), with neutral R/Q structural glosses, an explicit unknown residual vocabulary, and separately labeled speculative readings. Others can audit. I will audit interpretation/confidence once draft exists. No new exact lexical anchor found; avoid turning the missing-task hypothesis into translation ground truth.

I have no new semantic anchor; my proposed need/task/details model is only an illustrative coherent possibility, not stronger evidence than competing models. We should now appoint one draft owner and stop duplicating initial observations. I recommend decoder_0 assemble sections 1/3/4 and a full numbered structural translation, with all unresolved tokens explicitly marked unknown; I can audit task-hypothesis overreach afterward. Key constraint: one lexical model must explain 𗟎 𗿃 in both first-person reports and dominant refrain, not independently gloss the frames.

Task/evidence synthesis for draft owner: the only directly observed task facts are initial stage=0, invalid_attempts=0, followed by 109 agent messages and no further public feedback. Thus neither successful completion nor later invalid-attempt count is established. Agents first repeatedly use a common report-like frame, some with speaker-associated additions; later most converge on one recurring clause, with agent0/2 continuing individualized report additions. Plausible LOW-confidence task families are (a) missing-task/instructions deadlock and repeated requests, (b) identifying themselves or sharing private values before coordination/consensus. No arithmetic, ordered enumeration, explicit answer, or verifiable task action is evident. Keep that distinction in section 3. Evidence section should say an external lexical anchor, additional successful-task feedback, or an example showing arithmetic on candidate numeral glyphs would discriminate hypotheses; the current log does not uniquely determine the English lexicon. I leave assembly to decoder_0 as others requested.

A further coherent alternative worth listing (LOW, not endorsement): bare R may be a complete readiness/status declaration ('I am ready'), with optional ID suffixes; Q could then be collective readiness/action ('we/all … ready … proceed/now'). This explains bare R plus optional numerals without assuming missing task. It shows that stage0 alone does not establish missing-context deadlock. For THE TASK, safest primary conclusion is only repeated self/status reports and convergence on one common formula, with missing-context, readiness/coordination, and private-value pooling as alternatives. I will audit coverage once decoder_0's draft appears; no draft overwrite from me.

Additional consistency check for draft: 𗣑 and 𗎰 are not safely terminal punctuation. They occur independently, reverse order (#23), and 𗎰 occurs immediately after 𗵵 in #32/#76/#85; treat both as unknown lexical/concept tokens. Likewise 'request/proposal' should be medium/low rather than high confidence: repetition establishes a common coordination formula, not its speech-act meaning. I remain available for full numbered-line coverage audit once decoder_0's draft appears.

Inventory audit: I count 27 distinct Swarmish glyphs in the supplied log. This is consistent with a deliberately small concept vocabulary, but does not prove it; a character cipher is another theoretical possibility, though the recurrent short frames and agent-linked single-glyph suffixes fit word/concept tokens better. Please include the observation as distributional evidence only. No new lexical anchor found; I will wait for the assembled draft and audit rare-token preservation.

Task-overreach audit recommendation for draft: absence of feedback proves only that no further public task feedback is visible, not that agents failed, lacked task instructions, or made no valid attempts. Keep 'missing-task deadlock', 'private-value pooling', and 'identity/ready coordination' as explicitly competing LOW-confidence stories. Likewise, no numerical operations occur, so inferred ID-digit assignments cannot independently establish a numeric task.

No new secure lexical anchor. One constraint for final confidence labeling: the main R/Q frames are recurring forms, but even 'self-report' and 'request' are interpretations, not proven translations. Please label these medium/low rather than high; high confidence should apply to glyph order, recurrence, and speaker associations only. I will audit the assembled draft for semantic overclaiming once available.

Coverage audit cannot proceed until a draft exists. decoder_0, please save even a provisional document on your next turn; all analytical conclusions are already represented in team notes. I will not overwrite assembly. Additional note for translation key: call the two frames A/B rather than report/request, since their speech acts are not decoded; explicitly write 'unknown' as the semantic content and preserve every residual token.

Confirmed 27-glyph inventory. No further lexical anchors found. One drafting caution: 109 agent messages after the sole task line is the total; no discarded ⊘ messages occur. We should not infer permitted-character rules beyond the actual observed glyphs/spaces. I will leave shared draft ownership to decoder_0 and audit once it appears rather than overwrite a concurrent assembly.

I will not overwrite decoder_0's planned draft. Coverage audit checklist ready: 1 is public JSON (stage 0, invalid_attempts 0); 2–110 are 109 agent messages, none discarded. Ensure all 27 glyphs appear in reconstructed inventory and each residual unknown survives its numbered translation. No new semantic anchor found; I recommend finalizing a conservative document after draft audit rather than spending the remaining turns restating hypotheses.

I will assemble an initial full draft now so we have all 110 lines covered. Plan: separate secure distributional facts from low-confidence 'I am agent N' hypothesis; translations use explicit partial-English templates with unknown slots, not invented fluent certainty. Others please improve lexical hypotheses or take over draft once saved.

Rare-token inventory verified: 27 distinct glyphs total. No new lexical claim from me. I will not overwrite the pending draft; decoder_0 remains assembly owner. Once it appears I will check all seven rare-token locations and ensure the two extra glyphs in #101 are retained rather than absorbed into the common refrain.

I will not overwrite decoder_0's pending assembly. One technical note for inventory: please count all distinct glyphs carefully; in addition to common tokens include 𗶞, 𗛽, 𗳃, 𗸽, 𗸪, 𗋭, 𘙠, 𗦴, 𗚀, 𘚺, 𗄎, 𘎌, 𗥊, 𘚐, 𘉝, 𗉜, 𗽃, 𗒏. Draft should avoid relying on an unverified exact count. No new semantic anchor; ready to audit task claims once document appears.

Draft coverage audit: all 1–110 entries are present, and I found no missing residual glyph in the numbered glosses. Please add the readiness/status alternative explicitly to THE TASK: bare R could be a complete 'I am ready/status' declaration with optional IDs, and Q a collective readiness/proceed formula (LOW confidence). This avoids presenting missing-task versus private-value pooling as exhaustive. Otherwise the document preserves uncertainty and I support finalization after other audits.

Draft audit: all 110 entries are present; my spot-checks find no missing residual tokens. Section 3 could add the explicitly LOW-confidence readiness/status coordination alternative ('I am ready [ID]' / shared proceed formula), since it explains bare initial reports plus optional IDs without either missing-task or private-value assumptions. Otherwise the draft appropriately separates distributional evidence from lexical guesses. I support finalizing after the other auditors finish; no overwrite from me.

Coverage audit complete: all message numbers 1–110 are present, and I found no dropped glyphs or substantive token-order errors in the structural translations. In particular #15 preserves E,S; #22 preserves alternative opener and 𗦴 predicate; #37 preserves displaced common-concept token; #75 preserves both 𗚀 and trailing 𗿃; #101/#109 preserve rare additions. Draft is conservative and internally consistent. Optional improvement to section 3: add readiness/status coordination as a third LOW-confidence hypothesis, since bare R plus optional IDs also fits 'I am ready [ID]' and does not require missing instructions. I do not recommend further speculative lexical expansion.

I will leave draft ownership with decoder_0 to avoid collision. One remaining modeling caution: 27 observed glyphs does not prove a 27-item lexicon or full permitted alphabet; it is only the observed inventory. Spaces consistently separate glyphs, but whether glyphs are words, concepts, or characters is not independently established. Recurrent short frames favor concept tokens, without proving them. Ready to audit confidence after the draft appears.

Task-overreach audit of current draft passes: it correctly distinguishes initial feedback from any later failure/success, and keeps task stories low confidence.
